summary: Dolon is the forge of the Dominion: the court of the Dead Sea, ash kilns and salt-pans, black galleys on the storm coast, a ledger of its own, and a choice when the throne goes silent.

iron_steward.name: The Iron Steward
iron_steward.desc: Morvath keeps the ledgers of the Dominion in his own hand, and he keeps its forges in his own fist. A steward of iron is rarely kind, and always on time.

salt_council.name: The Salt Council
salt_council.desc: The salt-lords of the Dead Sea sit in a ring of grey benches and argue about every barrel. A council that argues so well rarely makes a bad bargain.

dead_sea_salt.name: Salt of the Dead Sea
dead_sea_salt.desc: Salt is raked from the pans in grey mounds, packed in barrels and sent north in the black galleys. It preserves meat, cures hides and pays for most things Dolon needs.

arms_of_dolon_spirit.name: The Arms of Dolon
arms_of_dolon_spirit.desc: Blades, spearheads and shield-bosses stamped with the mark of the Dead Sea go north in the hundreds. They are plain, heavy and unfailingly sound.

beyond_the_storms.name: Trade Beyond the Storms
beyond_the_storms.desc: Dolon's galleys, born under the storms, sail through them where other ships turn back. They carry salt and glass to coasts that the Dominion has never named.

own_crown.name: Dolon for Dolon
own_crown.desc: The Dead Sea has its own ledger now, and its own seal. Morvath signs in his own name, and the salt-lords write the date in their own calendar.

forges_never_rest_spirit.name: The Forges Never Rest
forges_never_rest_spirit.desc: Every forge in Dolon is lit night and day, and the glow of them can be seen from the Dead Sea itself. Workers sleep in shifts, and the anvils never cool.

dead_sea_court.title: The Court of the Dead Sea
dead_sea_court.desc: The salt-lords gather in the counting-house, with ledgers open and pens ready. Morvath enters, takes his seat and asks what is to be counted first.

silence_on_the_dead_sea.title: Silence on the Dead Sea
silence_on_the_dead_sea.desc: The black seals have stopped arriving, and the galleys wait in harbour for an order that does not come. What remains of the master of Nafeher, no one living can say.

focuses.name: The Court of the Dead Sea
focuses.desc: Morvath of the Dead Sea holds court in a counting-house as much as a throne room, with ledgers on every table and salt-lords on every bench. A court that counts everything is hard to cheat.

focuses.name: Morvath's Ledger
focuses.desc: Morvath keeps the Dominion's ledgers and a few of his own. Nobody has ever seen the second set, and everybody knows what they contain.

focuses.name: The Salt-Lords
focuses.desc: The salt-lords hold the pans and the barrel-yards, and their word on prices is final. They sit on grey benches at the court's left hand.

focuses.name: The Iron Steward
focuses.desc: Morvath takes the ledger and the seal into one hand. The salt-lords find that their votes have become a courtesy.

focuses.name: The Salt Council
focuses.desc: The salt-lords persuade Morvath to share the ledger with a council of their own. Every barrel now has three names on it.

focuses.name: Dolon Endures
focuses.desc: Whatever the Dominion asks, Dolon keeps its forges lit and its pans raked. The court proclaims that the land will endure, and the proclamation is written on a plate of black glass.

focuses.name: The Forges of Dolon
focuses.desc: The forges of Dolon arm the hosts of the Dominion, and every blade that goes north carries the mark of the Dead Sea. Morvath opens a new row of furnaces and counts the hours until they are lit.

focuses.name: Salt of the Dead Sea
focuses.desc: Grey mounds of salt line the shore of the Dead Sea, raked by hand and packed into barrels. It keeps meat for a year and a day, and the whole Dominion eats from it.

focuses.name: Ash Kilns
focuses.desc: Kilns of fired ash and clay are built beside the forges to bake the moulds. A well-made mould makes a hundred blades, and a hundred blades make a company.

focuses.name: Deep Salt-Pans
focuses.desc: New pans are dug deep into the salt flats, past the old brine-wells. They fill by hand and dry by sun, and every crust is worth a copper.

focuses.name: Arms for Nafeher
focuses.desc: Carts loaded with blades, spearheads and shield-bosses go north under Nafeher's seal. Ossira Forge-Mother signs for each one, and notes the count in the ash.

focuses.name: The Arms of Dolon
focuses.desc: The marks of Dolon are stamped on every blade, and the marks are known from the Dead Sea to the cold north. A smith who forges for Dolon forges for the whole Dominion.

focuses.name: Black Galleys
focuses.desc: Black galleys, pitched against the brine and rowed by crews born under the storms, are laid down on the Dead Sea shore. They sail where others will not, and come home with salt and silver.

focuses.name: Storm Wayfinders of Dolon
focuses.desc: Thuul of the Black Galleys teaches the wayfinders who steer through the storm coast, reading the waves like a script. A galley under such a hand reaches harbour when no one else does.

focuses.name: The Salt Harbour
focuses.desc: A harbour of grey stone is cut into the shore of the Dead Sea, with moles to break the storm swells. The galleys moor there in rows, and the salt-ships load beside them.

focuses.name: Galleys for the Dominion
focuses.desc: The galleys of Dolon are sent north to serve Nafeher, painted black and flying the Dominion's horned banner. Their crews are proud of it, and a little afraid.

focuses.name: The Storm-Harbour Chain
focuses.desc: A great chain, wrapped in tarred cloth against the salt, is stretched across the mouth of the harbour. No ship passes it uninvited, and few pass it in a storm.

focuses.name: A Ledger of Our Own
focuses.desc: Morvath opens a new book in the counting-house and starts to enter figures that the Dominion has never seen. It is a slow, patient and entirely lawful kind of rebellion.

focuses.name: Trade Beyond the Storms
focuses.desc: Dolon's galleys, born under the storms, sail through them where other ships turn back. They carry salt and glass to coasts that the Dominion has never named.

focuses.name: Quiet from Nafeher
focuses.desc: The seals from Nafeher grow fewer and the summons less urgent. Dolon's court is wise enough to use the quiet and not mention it.

focuses.name: A Steward of Salt
focuses.desc: Morvath names himself Steward of Salt, a title that belongs to no overlord. It is a small thing, written in a small hand, and it changes everything.

focuses.name: Dolon for Dolon
focuses.desc: Dolon raises its own banner: a black galley on a field of grey salt. It answers to the Dead Sea and to no throne beyond it.

focuses.name: Dolon Marches
focuses.desc: The war-horns of Dolon sound over the Dead Sea, and the forges are banked for the march. Every blade in the arsenal goes into a wagon, and every wagon goes north.

focuses.name: The Forges Never Rest
focuses.desc: Every forge in Dolon is lit night and day, and the glow of them can be seen from the Dead Sea itself. The smiths sleep in shifts, and the anvils never cool.

focuses.name: Shields of Dolon
focuses.desc: Dolon's shields are heavy, plain and unbreakable, and the Dominion's hosts march behind them. The smiths stamp each one with the black galley of the Dead Sea.

focuses.name: Dolon at Peace
focuses.desc: The war is over, and the forges slow to a walk. Morvath balances the ledger, pays the smiths and lets the galleys put to sea again.

focuses.name: A Throne That Does Not Answer
focuses.desc: The black-sealed letters no longer arrive from Nafeher. The Steward writes in a name that does not answer, and Morvath reads the letters twice and puts them in a drawer.

focuses.name: Stand with the Steward
focuses.desc: Morvath decides that Dolon's debts were owed to Nafeher, not to a name, and that Nafeher still stands. The Steward speaks for it, and Dolon's forges will serve the Steward's banner.

focuses.name: Free Dolon
focuses.desc: Morvath strikes out the Dominion's name from the ledger with a single stroke of the pen. Dolon is free, and the salt-lords drink to it standing.

focuses.name: Salt and Iron Endure
focuses.desc: Salt and iron are still salt and iron, whoever holds the seal. The forges burn on, the pans fill and the galleys sail on with the tide.
